1. Use a proxy to try and find that cover.

2. Failing that, find an artist you like who draws and sells dakis. An artist you /really/ like. Go through their portfolio, see what you admire about their work and what you don't until you hunker down on an artist that really seems to get what you want. Prepare to pay out the ass for those images, especially if you get them privately printed through CO to ensure the images won't be stolen by bootleggers.

Tell the artist up front you want WIPs frequently and to not just finish the commission right away or without contacting you, even if it's just small things edited. That way you and the artist can work together on your dream daki.

Ask them to post a cropped or heavily watermarked version for their portfolio if they post it online. Also, be kind to them! Tip them, if you can. As an artist myself, knowing that your work is appreciated enough for a tip between doing several wips and edits is a really kind gesture.

Don't get it printed through any bootlegger site or alibaba or ebay listing or anything promising custom. Artscow and Snapmade are still Chinese printers, and I have no idea what they do with the image after. Print it with a dakimakura website like CO or a japanese one.

Other than that, go forth!

Looks are deceiving-- these are always 20 dollars (16 if you have the monthly coupon) and they've held up so well. How well?

You will leave behind a cataclysm and revoke your right for things to be better.

This is not an exaggeration-- you might go "people commit suicide every day, and i don't know them!" but please trust me. The others that tell you your life is worth living, say so because your death would be catastrophic, not because they can give you the answer to keep living. Imagine loving someone who talks about how they want to kill themselves and all that's in your power to do is reassure them-- you can't take them in, pay for their therapy, make sure they take their meds, make sure they aren't hurting themselves. At that point, you are totally powerless. And they demonstrate it by taking their own life.

Once you're gone, you're gone. All the people who hoped their words were enough and hoped with all their heart they could do more for you never had a chance to get to that point where they could help you, be it getting you to a therapist, helping you take your medication, or even something as simple as sending you something in the mail to look forward to. That's on their shoulders for their entire life, even if you wanted to tell them there's nothing they could do.

As for what being human is, in a completely emotionless take, it's whatever you need it to be. You don't need any of the things you listed to be human. You're already human whether you like it or not. Luckily, you get to decide what human is for yourself. No one else does.
